chapter_title: Concept of Mole and Chemical Calculation

sections.content_markdown:
The word mole is the unit of any chemical measurement. Suppose,

$$12 \text{ nos of } \text{O}_2 = 1 \text{ dozen of } \text{O}_2$$
$$100 \text{ nos of } \text{O}_2 = 1 \text{ hundred of } \text{O}_2$$
$$1000 \text{ nos of } \text{O}_2 = 1 \text{ thousand of } \text{O}_2$$

Similarly, $6.023 \times 10^{23} \text{ nos } \text{O}_2 = 1 \text{ mole } \text{O}_2$

$1 \text{ mole atom contains } 6.02 \times 10^{23} \text{ atoms}$
$1 \text{ mole molecule contains } 6.02 \times 10^{23} \text{ molecules}$
$1 \text{ mole ion contains } 6.02 \times 10^{23} \text{ ions}$

Therefore, the number $6.02 \times 10^{23}$ is used in the case with atoms, molecules and ions etc. This number is called the Avogadro number.

The amount of a chemical substance that contains as many as the Avogadro number ($6.02 \times 10^{23}$) of molecules, atoms or ions is called the mole of the substance. For example, $12 \text{ grams of C}$ contains $6.02 \times 10^{23}$ number of $\text{C}$ atoms.

The expression of atomic mass of atoms and the molecular mass of molecules into gram unit is called one mole of a chemical substance. Therefore,

$$12 \text{ grams of C} = 1 \text{ mole C atom.}$$

Again, $18 \text{ grams of } \text{H}_2\text{O}$ contains $6.02 \times 10^{23}$ number of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ molecules. Therefore,

$$18 \text{ grams of } \text{H}_2\text{O} = 1 \text{ mole } \text{H}_2\text{O}.$$

sections.section_title: The Process of Determining the Molecular Mass of a Molecule
sections.content_markdown:
The summation of atomic masses of all atoms that constitute a molecule denotes the molecular mass of the molecule. $\text{Cl}_2$ molecule, for example, has two $\text{Cl}$ atoms.

Therefore, the molecular mass of $\text{Cl}_2 = \text{atomic mass of Cl} \times 2 = 2 \times 35.5 = 71$

$$\text{One mole } \text{Cl}_2 = 71 \text{ g } \text{Cl}_2.$$
